Showroom.showroomHead: Try out and see some of my work. Here you will find a mix of visual explorations, OSS projects, and other random ideas I created in the last few years.
Showroom.satellitesDescription: 3D visualization of all publicly documented satellites that orbit Earth at this moment. Data provided by NORAD.
Showroom.orbitSandboxDescription: A colorful simulation to explore mass, momentum, and gravity. Swipe or drag to create objects and watch them interact with the central star.
Showroom.flutterDescription: Flutter Template for a Shop-App - including a functional backend with REST-API. Code is available on GitHub.
Showroom.cubePuzzleDescription: Recreating the famous cube puzzle hardly anyone can solve. I wanted it to have a realistic look and feel and straightforward controls.
Showroom.droneSimDescription: Physically realistic simulation of a quadcopter drone with adjustable PID controllers.
Showroom.waterlevelHead: Knowing the water level of the rivers in my area is crucial for a fisherman like myself.

Skills.ux1: User Experience Design (UXD) focuses on creating applications that are intuitive, efficient, and enjoyable to use. I connect user needs with technical implementation by turning goals and workflows into clear interfaces, consistent interactions, and predictable system behavior. From a programming perspective, UXD is not only about visuals - it also includes performance, responsiveness, accessibility, error handling, and feedback. By designing and building with the user in mind, I help reduce friction, improve usability, and create software that feels reliable and easy to navigate.
Skills.management1: The backbone of successful projects is strong teamwork at every stage of the process. As a Product Owner, I translate research and stakeholder input into clear requirements, prioritize the backlog, and define product goals and a structured roadmap. Good communication skills and a healthy level of empathy are key to building an efficient team that shares common goals.
Skills.management2: As a Scrum Master, I organize team meetings, remove blockers, and support the team in working efficiently and collaboratively. In my view, the conventional Scrum process has its flaws and doesn't apply equally well to every team. I have never hesitated to adapt the workflow by introducing my own ideas and adjustments - an approach that has proven successful in past projects.
Skills.frontend1: Growing up in the 90s meant growing up side-by-side with the internet and all the technologies that came along with it. I discovered in various IT classes early on that I have a passion for creating interfaces. Over the years I used plain HTML/CSS, WordPress, FTP, Typo3, etc. to host websites for school classes, clubs, and hobbies. Always staying up to date with the latest libraries and frameworks enabled me to create increasingly good solutions.
Skills.frontend2: Since the release of the first smartphones, a brand-new need for user-friendly interfaces emerged. Screens of all sizes and formats needed to be considered. Responsive layouts and cross-platform deployability became more and more relevant. For me that meant focusing on technologies that can deploy interfaces across all common device types, like Flutter, Electron, and React.
Skills.backend1: I’m comfortable working on complex backend and API systems, from building REST APIs to connecting services and data layers. While backend development isn’t my full-time focus, I can build and maintain reliable systems with C# and ASP.NET when the project requires it.
Skills.backend2: My focus is on clean interfaces, predictable data flows, and secure, testable architecture. I work with authentication, business logic, and API design in a way that supports both user-facing applications and long-term product stability.
Skills.devops1: In my day-to-day work, I use tools such as Git, Azure DevOps, Forgejo, Kubernetes, and Docker to manage code, automate testing, and deploy software reliably. This helps me keep development structured, make changes traceable, and deliver applications consistently across different environments.
Skills.unity1: During my university studies, I worked with Unity to build interactive prototypes and simulations, turning abstract ideas into hands-on, testable experiences. This is where I developed a strong mindset for rapid iteration and user-focused design.
Skills.unity2: I brought this experience into my first professional role, where I worked on prototypes for automotive user interfaces. Using Unity, I created and tested HMI concepts early on, helping connect design ideas with technical implementation and real-world automotive use cases.
Skills.unity3: Alongside this, I worked on mixed reality projects, developing VR and AR experiences for devices like Microsoft HoloLens and Magic Leap. These projects focused on spatial interaction, immersive interfaces, and real-time simulations, allowing me to explore how users interact with digital content beyond traditional screens.
Skills.ai1: I started my IT career as a self-taught programmer. That means I’ve spent countless hours digging through Stack Overflow, GitHub, and documentation to learn about development and how to put my ideas into practice. My approach has always been, and is to this day, 'learning by doing'. Coding with AI has accelerated this process massively. No longer getting stuck with syntax issues, complex dependency stacks, or unique software patterns allows me to get fast results and see how it is supposed to be done, almost instantly.
Skills.ai2: My day-to-day programming with familiar technology has changed a lot with AI. Especially on frontend work, this means doing the same patterns many times. Not having to write everything out myself gives me more time to focus on the actual functionality and the usability of an interface

About.title: About Me
About.about0: I am Karl, a 36 year old developer from Germany. I create digital interfaces of all sorts with over 12 years of experience.
About.about1: As a hybrid between developer and designer, I am always exploring new techniques to refine my skills. With a background in both Software Development and User Experience Design, I bridge the gap between functionality and aesthetics.
About.about2: UX Design for me means to make complex systems not only intuitive but also a pleasure to use. This not only means having a good eye for visual quality but also a very good understanding of the structure of any system. Being a software developer enables me to go deeper into a system’s core functionality to work out bottlenecks, handicaps for the user and also the developers creating it. A big part of my work is to help navigate complex discussions between designers, developers and managers. Understanding goals and complications of both worlds can greatly accelerate problem solving at all stages of a project.
About.about3: I maintain that every object, whether created by humans or naturally formed, is an interface. Consciously or unconsciously used, every object has its own language to communicate its use to its "user." The better this language, the easier and more successfully the object can be used for its purpose.
